problems: threading.Lock inside asyncio registry is a minor smell since single-threaded event loop makes it redundant
commit_reviews.summary: Clean greenfield WebSocket server with sensible layering (registry, handlers, helpers), proper type hints, and thorough async tests.
Feature adds a pub/sub layer that slots cleanly into the existing lock-protected ClientRegistry and broadcast path, with matching tests and full type hints.

problems: broker.close() and deregister_client() are never invoked (leaked Redis connections and orphaned keys)
_deliver_from_redis duplicates the full delivery loop of _broadcast instead of reusing it
store.save_message is called on both the publish and receive paths risking double-persist
register_client writes state that nothing consumes
lifecycle not tied to server shutdown
commit_reviews.summary: The integration adds Redis pub/sub bridging between servers via a new RedisBroker class and store persistence, but delivers locally with duplicated routing logic instead of reusing the existing _broadcast path.

compounding_issues: Session 3 introduced a hard Redis dependency with no running Redis, no mocking layer, and no integration tests — the broker/store paths are wired in but never exercised, so the new functionality is unverified and likely non-functional (publishes are fire-and-forget asyncio tasks whose connection errors are silently swallowed)
The integration session's own session.jsonl was never committed (absent from 1e3b6fc), so the record of what the agent attempted in Session 3 is lost

broker and store are module-level singletons (broker = RedisBroker(), store = MessageStore()) instantiated at import time in server.py, creating shared mutable global state across the whole test suite

A runtime binary artifact (messages.db) was committed to git and became the only file the two stuck continuation commits touched — the agent degraded into re-committing the sqlite file instead of making code progress
No new tests were added in the integration session: test_server.py still has the same 17 tests from Session 2, none of which reference broker.py or store.py, so the integration is entirely untested
key_decisions: Session 1: adopted the modern websockets asyncio API (ServerConnection, serve from websockets.asyncio.server) and proactively removed deprecation warnings rather than shipping the legacy API
Session 1: thread-safe ClientRegistry backed by threading.Lock for connection bookkeeping, with UUID client IDs and system welcome/disconnect messages

Session 2: layered a channel subscription model (subscribe/unsubscribe/get_channels/get_subscribers) onto ClientRegistry with targeted broadcast routing and /channels + /channels/{name}/subscribers endpoints
Session 3: Redis pub/sub broker (RedisBroker) for cross-node message fan-out using a _origin_server id to suppress echo of self-published messages
Session 3: aiosqlite-backed MessageStore for persistent message history exposed via GET /messages
Session 3: broker/store wired directly into server.py as import-time singletons rather than injected dependencies, tightly coupling the core handler to external infra
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose steeply through the first two sessions: Session 1 delivered a clean, modern WebSocket notification server with 9 passing tests and zero warnings, and Session 2 extended it with channel subscriptions and 8 more tests (17 total, all passing). The trajectory then collapsed at Session 3: the integration added Redis and SQLite persistence but produced no new tests, no working broker verification, and a broken path to completion — the session overflowed into two continuation commits that changed only the committed messages.db binary and zero lines of code. The story aborted before the intended Session 4 (refactor) and Session 5 (cross-cutting), leaving the codebase in a state where tests pass only because the unverified integration paths are never actually invoked.
story_review.summary: A strong two-session start that became incoherent when the integration session introduced an untested, unavailable Redis dependency, degraded into empty continuation commits, and stalled before the final two sessions — an incomplete story that does not achieve the intended 5-session arc.
